question.leadin: He was killed near the end of a June 1876 battle in the Montana territory.
question.text: Name that 7th Cavalry commander famous for his "last stand."
question.clue: The Battle of the Rosebud prevented George Crook from joining up with this man, who was killed by the forces of Sitting Bull.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about U.S. government relations with Native Americans in the late 19th century.
swap.text: At this 1876 battle, George Custer's 7th Cavalry Regiment was annihilated by the forces of Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse.
swap.clue: Recounts of this battle often feature the Lone Teepee, and leaders on one side were Frederick Benteen and Marcus Reno.

question.leadin: John Altgeld pardoned Oscar Neebe, Michael Schwab, and Samuel Fielden for their roles in this event.
question.text: Name this 1886 disturbance in which eleven people were killed during a labor rally at the McCormick Harvesting Machine Company plant.
question.clue: The main action of this event interrupted a speech on socialism delivered by Samuel Fielden, and its aftermath saw the pardon of three of its conspirators by John Peter Altgeld.

swap.leadin: This act, along with the Geary Act renewing this act for another decade, was the subject of an apologetic 2012 House resolution.
swap.text: Name this discriminatory law, signed by Chester Arthur in 1882 and repealed in 1943, that banned immigration from a certain Asian nation but did not restrict immigration of other races.
swap.clue: It sought to protect the wage level, since people felt that many were working on the Transcontinental Railroad for too low of a wage.

question.leadin: This scandal involved the construction of the Union Pacific railroad.
question.text: Oakes Ames offered discounted shares in a namesake construction company to other congressmen in this scandal. It took place during the building of the Transcontinental Railroad.
question.clue: Peter A. Day was fired for providing ungenerous estimates in this scandal, while James Brooks was censured in the investigation following its exposure.

swap.text: Two years prior, German U-boats sank the Lusitania, which caused this Secretary of State to resign. This former populist presidential candidate claimed "you shall not crucify mankind" upon the title object in one speech.
swap.clue: He was cross-examined by Clarence Darrow during the Scopes Trial.

question.text: After being imprisoned for his drag balls, Swann petitioned this President for a pardon. After he had an illegitimate child with Maria Halpin, this President was targeted with the chant "Ma, Ma, where's my Pa."
question.clue: This man used federal troops to put down the Pullman Strike.

swap.leadin: This organization was formed by disgruntled members of the Knights of Labor in 1886.
swap.text: Name this labor union that was founded by Samuel Gompers in Columbus, Ohio. George Meany later led this union when it merged with the CIO in 1955.
swap.clue: At its founding in 1886, this organization elected its first president, Samul Gompers.

question.leadin: Name these American third parties from presidential candidates.
question.text: Eugene Chafin, Clinton Fisk, John Bidwell
question.clue: They allowed Grover Cleveland to carry New York with the strong 1884 showing of John St. John, but their best results came in the next two presidential elections, in which Clinton Fisk and John Bidwell polled over 200,000 votes.

swap.leadin: It was investigated independently by Treasury Secretary Benjamin Bristow.
swap.text: Identify this criminal organization active during the Grant administration, centered in the midwest, that siphoned millions of dollars off of various illegal activities involving an alcoholic substance.
swap.clue: John B Henderson whom the president appointed as the special, prosecutor, was tried the accused.

question.leadin: In 1896, this future Georgian senator was seriously considered as a possible running mate for William Jennings Bryan on the Democratic platform.
question.text: As a representative, this man tried to require the Postal Service to deliver to rural areas for free, and he earned black support by condemning lynching, but was later prosecuted for his anti-Catholic newsletters.
question.clue: This editor of The Jefersonian covered the bejesus out of Frank's trial, because he wanted to use it to revive the Ku Klux Klan. This Georgia politician was the Populist Party nominee for President in both 1904 and 1908, afer which the party dis-banded.

swap.leadin: This labor union was the first to advocate one union for all workers.
swap.text: Name this labor group founded in 1869 by Uriah Stephens, which was ultimately supplanted by Samuel Gompers' craft union, the American Federation of Labor.
swap.clue: This organization's first Grand Master Workman was Uriah Stephens, who was succeeded by Terence Powderley.

question.text: In response to the later decision Wabash v. Illinois that restricted states' authority to regulate railroads, Congress established this first independent regulatory agency.
question.clue: This organization had its power strengthened by the Hepburn and Mann Elkins Act, which regulated "unfair trade practices".

swap.text: Atheist Michael Newdow argued that this commonly recited statement in schools was a prayer because it used the phrase "under God." The Supreme Court has ruled that students do not need to stand up or salute the flag while this statement is being read.
swap.clue: In 1943, Jehovah's Witnesses argued that engaging in this practice constituted veneration in the landmark case West Virginia vs. Barnette.

question.leadin: Learmonth Dalrymple, a prominent member of this organization, pushed to found Otago's first secondary school for girls.
question.text: Name this international organization. A founding member of its New Zealand branch, Kate Sheppard, pushed heavily for Lord Glasgow to pass a law granting women's suffrage in New Zealand.
question.clue: This group, which used the slogan "For God and Home and Every Land" and was led by Annie Wittenmyer, adopted a Xenophon quote to argue for "total abstinence from everything harmful."

swap.leadin: Name these people who ran for president of the United State with third parties in the nineteenth century.
swap.text: This inventor and owner of an epic beard manufactured the first American locomotive and ran for president with the Greenback party in 1876.
swap.clue: He obtained a patent for gelatin which he sold to Pearl Wait who invented the name Jell-O.

question.leadin: Tyler Anbinder notes how the description of this person by New York Times as "a little rosy-cheeked Irish girl" selectively ignored her fellow passengers primarily from Eastern and Southern Europe.
question.text: Name this teen who, on New Year's Day, 1892, became the first registered immigrant at Ellis Island.

swap.text: In the drawing "Woman: The Eternal Question," Gibson depicts this model with her hair falling into the shape of a question mark. In a later incident, she described kicking a parasol while sitting on a "red velvet swing" in a 24th Street apartment.
swap.answerHtml: Evelyn Nesbit (the "red velvet swing" incident refers to her first trip to Stanford White's apartment)

question.text: While this woman was involved with temperance, she was better known for her work with the Populist Party. She is credited with saying "you farmers need to raise less corn and more hell."
question.clue: This Irish-American itinerant orator and staunch supporter of presidential candidate James Weaver. She apocryphally told farmers to "raise less corn and more hell."

swap.text: This sharpshooter briefly joined Buffalo Bill's Wild West show, but left because of alcoholism. The dime novels of Edward Wheeler popularized the myth of this figure's connection to Deadwood Dick.
swap.clue: This frontierswoman also joined the Wild West show, but her fame was mostly due to her being a character in the Deadwood Dick dime novels, which made her an icon of the Wild West. While considered a fierce fighter, this woman was renowned for her kindness and for aiding strangers in need.
